title: Access features: inlet, outlet, overflow, edges and depth
audience: Pond and water-feature technicians who inspect and service the inlet, outlet, overflow, edges and depth of an existing pond
learningOutcomes: Describe the job of the inlet, outlet, overflow and drain point, and check each for blockage, movement or leaks
Measure freeboard and water depth at a fixed reference point, and record them so that later changes can be seen
Inspect pond edges, stones and banks for movement, soil wash-in and exposed liner, and make the area safe
Identify tree-root, erosion and bank problems, and refer repair work without cutting roots near the liner

instruction.heading: Access is part of the job
instruction.body: A pond service is only as good as the access to the parts that need attention. The pump, the filter, the skimmer, the valves, the outlet, the overflow and any drain point all need to be reachable without stepping on the liner, without lifting heavy stones alone and without working over deep water. Before a visit, check the access route and any path the owner has asked you to keep clear, and note any part that cannot be reached safely. A new pond or a new excavation is a separate course and is not part of this lesson. This lesson covers checking and maintaining the access features of a pond that already exists.

instruction.heading: Inlet, outlet and overflow
instruction.body: The inlet returns water to the pond, usually from a pump or a filter. The outlet draws water out, for example to a skimmer, a pump intake or a drain point. The overflow lets excess water leave during heavy rain, so that the water level stays below the rim. Inspect each in turn. Check that the outlet has its screen in place, because a suction screen keeps fish, animals and debris out of the pipe. Remove any blockage with the power off and the pump isolated. Look for cracks, loose joints and movement where a pipe passes through the liner, and check that the inlet return still points where it was set. Check where the overflow water goes, and confirm that the discharge point is the one the owner has agreed. One NSW council's stormwater factsheet treats putting stormwater into its sewer as an offence, and it does not mention pond water. The route must be checked before any water is discharged.

instruction.heading: Freeboard and water level
instruction.body: Freeboard is the vertical gap between the water surface and the lowest point of the pond rim or edge. The water should never run over the top, so the freeboard should stay clear at all times, including during heavy rain. Measure it at a fixed point and record the value in millimetres, with the date. Add a permanent reference mark on a wall or a fixed feature if the owner agrees, so that the next measurement is taken from the same place. A fall in water level is a reason to run a bucket test, as set out in the liner lesson (“Pond liner and leak inspection”). A rise that brings the water close to the rim calls for an overflow check and a note to the owner.

instruction.heading: Edges, banks and exit points
instruction.body: The edges hold the liner in place and hide it from view. Check that edge stones, slabs and pavers are firm, that none has shifted to expose the liner, and that soil or sand is not washing into the pond along the edge. Where a drainage strip of coarse gravel has been used at the edge, check that it is still free of soil. Stones that are fist-sized or larger, piled to hold steep slopes, are the usual approach to securing an edge in a garden pond, and a loose stone on a steep bank is a fall and crush hazard. Make the area safe before you work on a bank. Check that there is a way out for animals and for people, such as a gently sloped section or an exit aid, because steep, smooth walls can trap animals that fall in. Note wet edges and slippery areas on the record.

instruction.heading: Depth, sediment and the bank zone
instruction.body: Depth is recorded at the same reference point each time, with a marked pole or a measured line. Record the depth to the sediment as well as the depth of the water, because the difference shows how fast sediment is building up, which links to the sludge work in “Debris, sludge and plant management”. Keep the shallow margins, where many animals live, in good condition and free of debris, and do not make them deeper without the owner's agreement. Depth also matters for winter refuge, which is covered in “Seasonal care and cold-climate notes”.

instruction.heading: Trees, roots and embankments
instruction.body: Tree roots can push under the liner or lift the edge, and leaf fall adds to the load in the pond. Where a root is under or next to the liner, record its location, photograph it where the business requires, and refer the repair. In an embankment pond, the bank is a dike, and its job is to hold the water. Check for erosion, bare patches, wet spots, cracks and animal burrows, and check that grass or other ground cover is still holding the bank. Large trees on or near a dike are a risk to its structure, so note them in the record and refer any concern to the owner. Do not cut roots close to the liner.

procedure: Confirm the access route and any parts the owner has asked you to keep clear.
Isolate the pump before clearing any blockage at the outlet, the intake or the overflow, and prove it off.
Check the outlet screen, the inlet return and the overflow route, and record any blockage or movement.
Measure freeboard and water depth at the fixed reference point, and record sediment depth at the same point.
Inspect edge stones, slabs and pavers for movement, soil wash-in and exposed liner, and make the area safe before working on any bank.
Check the bank and any tree roots near the liner, and record the location of each concern.
Refer any repair, tree work or structural concern to the owner in writing, with the measurements taken.

workedExamples.situation: An overflow pipe is partly blocked by leaves, and the water is rising towards the top edge after rain.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the best first action?
workedExamples.reasoning: Isolate any pump that could draw debris into the pipe, then clear the blockage safely from the outside of the pond. Measure the freeboard and record it, check where the overflow water goes, and tell the owner that the blockage has been cleared and the freeboard before and after. Do not seal the overflow, because that would let the water rise over the rim.

workedExamples.situation: A stone on a steep bank has shifted, and a section of liner is visible at the edge.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop lifting or stepping on the bank. Keep people and pets away from the edge, record the location and a photograph, and refer the repair to the owner. Do not move the stone alone, and do not walk on the liner to reach it. The record shows the danger, the referral and the time.

equipmentAndPpe: Marked depth pole or measuring line with a fixed reference point
Gloves, eye protection and footwear with grip as set by {{business:safety.required_ppe}}
Access and defect record form or system

commonErrors.error: Sealing or raising the overflow instead of clearing it.
commonErrors.prevention: Clear the blockage safely, measure the freeboard and record the result.

commonErrors.error: Working on a steep bank without making the area safe.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, keep people clear, record the hazard and refer the repair.

commonErrors.error: Cutting tree roots near the liner.
commonErrors.prevention: Record and photograph the root and refer the repair.

commonErrors.error: Measuring depth or freeboard at a different point each visit.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the same reference point, and record it on the form.

commonErrors.error: Leaving an outlet screen missing after a clean.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the screen is in place before leaving the pond.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Edges, banks and steep slopes create slip, fall and crush risks. Make the area safe before working on a bank, and never work alone on a loose stone on a steep bank.
Confirm the route with the owner and the council before any water is discharged (see “Water conservation and environmental release for ponds”).
Tree work, including root cutting near a pond, may need the owner's agreement and approval. This lesson does not authorise tree work.

Any electrical outlet, pump or fitting near the access point must be isolated and proven off before work. Electrical repair is for a licensed person where the rules require it; in NSW, wiring work is licensed or certified work at any price (see “Pumps, UV clarifiers and filters” and “Electrical, mechanical and confined-space boundaries for ponds”).

qualityStandard: Freeboard, water depth and sediment depth are measured at the fixed reference point and recorded
Outlet screen, inlet return and overflow route are checked and any blockage is cleared with the pump isolated
Edge hazards and root concerns are recorded and referred before the visit ends
documentationEvidence: Access and depth record with the reference point, the freeboard, the water depth and the sediment depth
Blockage or defect record with location, photographs where required, and the action taken
Referral note for any repair, tree concern or structural issue
summary: The inlet, outlet, overflow and drain point each need inspection for blockage, movement and leaks.
Freeboard should stay clear at all times, so measure it at a fixed point and record it.
Edges and banks are a slip, fall and crush hazard, and loose stones are referred, not moved alone.
Do not cut tree roots near the liner, and refer tree work and any discharge route to the owner and the council.

knowledgeChecks.question: An overflow pipe is partly blocked by leaves, and the water is rising towards the top edge. What is the best first action?
options: Clear the blockage safely after isolating any pump that could draw debris into the pipe, then check the freeboard and the overflow route
Raise the water level so the overflow is covered by the water, which keeps the pond full and stops any leaf from blocking the pipe later
Seal the overflow so the water cannot escape, which keeps the pond level and stops any leaking outflow from the pipe
Leave it until the next scheduled visit, since the pond is not in danger yet and the rain will ease off by the weekend

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should the edge stones of a steep bank be checked during a visit?
options: They control the pH of the water in the pond and the bank
They can shift, expose the liner, or let soil wash into the pond
They must be removed every season and reset by the crew
They add dissolved oxygen to the water from the bank edge

knowledgeChecks.question: A tree root is pushing under the liner close to a pond edge. What should the technician do?
options: Cut the root with a saw close to the liner, since the root is in the way of the repair
Record and photograph the damage, and refer the repair without cutting roots near the liner
Cover the root with more gravel and move on to the next job without any further checks today
Pull the root out by hand firmly, since it is only a thin root near the edge of the liner
